editorial.description_en: What is underfoot in a wood — leaf litter, moss and shade averaged into one colour.
editorial.description_ja: 林の地面のような、暗い黄緑。

provenance.derivation: Editorial construction, not a measurement. Specified in OKLCh as L 0.418, C 0.060, h 136.0° and converted to canonical D65 XYZ by @irodora/color-spaces 0.1.0 (oklchToXyz), rounded to six decimal places. Re-derivable from this sentence alone.
provenance.editorialNotes: Name coined by Irodora: 林 (rin, wood) + 床 (shō, floor), the standing term for the forest floor. It is not asserted to be a traditional Japanese colour name, and the hyphenated romaji marks it as a constructed compound (ADR-0065). "Forest Floor" is an editorial decision about what communicates in English, not a literal translation of 林床. Relations asserted from measured proximity under the current engine, not from a source: related is the three nearest in CIELAB — numa-kage at ΔE00 6.2, iwa-goke at ΔE00 7.0, tetsu-midori at ΔE00 8.5. complementary is empty because no entry in this corpus sits within 22° of the opposite hue. historicalVariants is empty: this entry makes no historical claim to vary from.
